content:
maya: Heads-up — we observed a client hitting sustained 5k req/s burst and our ingress queue grew to ~12k entries, ended up returning a bunch of 503s from the proxy. Any thoughts on if we should prefer 429 vs 503 for request-shed?

liam: 503s are noisy for customers. 429 signals rate limiting. But 429 implies client should retry with backoff — that's good if they respect Retry-After.

sophie: Per-key quotas right now are token-bucket w/burst 2x, per-org uses leaky-bucket at infra layer. The issue is we hit global queue depth cap then proxy returns 503 from nginx before quota check.

ahmed: We can reorder checks: quota/check token at edge and immediately 429 if over. That avoids heavy queueing. Downside: we lose per-org aggregated fairness if requests arrive through multiple edge nodes.

maya: Good point. Also need to think about short-lived spikes from SDK retries — 429 might cause retry storms unless we set Retry-After and jitter.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/edge-rate-check landed in canary (region-us-west) — rolling 10% -> 25% -> 50%. (ci:build/4829)

liam: For burst controls, what about token-bucket with a shared global reserve for orgs on paid tiers? Reserve used until exhaustion then fall back to per-key bucket.

sophie: That works but telemetry must expose "reserve used" and "burst credits remaining" per-org in console. We currently only show "requests/sec" and rejected count.

maya: UX ask: console should show per-route quota + current window consumption + burst headroom. Ops wants alert on "queue depth > 5k for 1m".

ahmed: Implementation idea: perform cheap pre-check at L7 edge — check rate-limiter cache (local redis ring) then fast-reject 429 w/Retry-After if exceeded; accepted requests proceed to queue which enforces concurrency and longer-term fairness. If internal queue can't accept, return 503 (overloaded).

liam: So two-stage: 429 for quota breach, 503 for transient infra overload. That feels correct semantically.

sophie: Need to be careful: SDKs often interpret 503 as retryable w/o backoff hints, 429 sometimes not handled properly. We should prioritize using Retry-After header for both, but different guidance in docs.

maya: Can we put a header X-Redwood-Reason: quota | overload to help customers? Also expose metric labels reason=quota/overload for traces.

ahmed: Agree. Also add a counter metric: shed_total{reason="quota"} and shed_total{reason="overload"}, and histogram for latency of pre-check.

liam: What about per-key vs per-org limits? If per-key is over but org has headroom, do we allow fallback? Risk: one key monopolizes org headroom — policy should be configurable: "strict-key" default = true for security.

sophie: For canary let's default strict-key=true and test metrics. If customers opt-in, they can set "allow-org-burst=true".

maya: Any concern about cross-region syncing of token buckets? We keep per-edge buckets and occasionally sync usage. That allows short bursts per region — acceptable.

ahmed: Also we should implement queue-shedding strategy prioritizing SDK connections with ephemeral session tokens lower than long-lived ones? Hmm maybe overkill.

liam: Ops: how do we alert on misconfiguration loops? e.g., clients keep getting 429 -> immediate retry -> more 429s. Suggest synthetic tests in canary to detect retry loops.

maya: Action items:
- implement edge pre-check + Retry-After header (ahmed)
- add X-Redwood-Reason header (liam)
- console: per-route quota + burst headroom + queue depth alerts (sophie)
- docs: update retry guidance for 429 vs 503 and SDK behaviour (maya)
- canary rollout: strict-key=true default (deploy-bot will schedule)

deploy-bot: deploy note: canary started 10:12 PST, region-us-west-1 -> 10% traffic.

ahmed: I'll open a PR with pre-check patch and metrics. Link: http://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/542

sophie: I'll prototype console widgets; need backend telemetry endpoint. Ping me if you need labels.

maya: Thanks team. Let's regroup after canary 24h.
